title: Wolfram: The AI Revolution and Implications to Project Catalyst

ms.promise: Two outputs: 1) A report summarizing the literature review in a PDF file and 2) A report summarizing community surveys in a PDF file.
ms.criteria:
Our goal with surveys is to learn what the general level of understanding of LLMs is from the Catalyst community AND to gather feedback from the Catalyst community about what they imagine would be useful from an LLM. 
The literature review should increase the community's level of understanding of LLMs and can indicate what use cases are possibly attainable.
ms.report:
The project has two outputs:
・Literature Review Report: A PDF document that provides an in-depth review of existing literature related to Large Language Models (LLMs). This report aims to enhance the community's understanding of LLMs and outline potential use cases.
・Community Survey Report: A PDF document summarizing surveys conducted within the Catalyst community. The purpose is to gauge the community's current understanding of LLMs and collect their perspectives on how LLMs could be beneficially utilized.

The acceptance criteria for these outputs are as follows:
・The community surveys should reveal the general understanding of LLMs within the Catalyst community and collect feedback on potential uses and expectations for LLMs.
・The literature review should deepen the community's understanding of LLMs and highlight possible applications that align with community interests and needs.

The evidence of milestone completion will be a short video demonstrating and walking through the contents of both the literature review and community surveys.

ms.promise: The output will be a collection in github of the data collection, documentation, and resources that would go into this process.
ms.criteria: A public github collection of relevant Catalyst data/content/documentation that would be used in the evaluation process.
ms.report:
Milestone 2 has the following outputs:
・A collection in github of the data collection, documentation, and resources that went into this process, including:
・Complete Fund 1-11 Catalyst data demonstrated in the PDF Report 
・Complete (structured and merged) full proposal data demonstrated in the PDF Report
・Transcripts from livestreams of Charles Hoskinson demonstrated in the PDF Report
・Voting data from Funds 5-11 and a process for exploring voting power demonstrated in the PDF Report
・A video recap from a town hall breakout room is not included here because this milestone was completed during the post Fund 11 cool down period. Instead, we gathered and recorded this community event to discuss research related to this project.
・A town hall breakout room will be added and uploaded to the PDF Report when the cool down period has ended, assuming mid-April. 

The acceptance criteria for this output is as follows:
・A public github collection of relevant Catalyst data/content/documentation that would be used in the evaluation process.

The evidence of milestone completion will be:
・A short video demonstrating and walking through the contents of the data collection in github and a supplemental PDF report with additional key resources.

Important clarifying note: github is not the best public place for datasets to exist, which is why we put the instructions on github for accessing the data which point to the datasets outside of github.

ms.promise:
A PDF report to the community including:
・Review different LLMs, narrowing the choices for the optimal LLM for the Catalyst use case

Also, conduct a discussion of results in an after town hall breakout room with community to ensure feedback.
ms.criteria: Determine the list of potential LLM models that could be used for this research via evaluations. Choose the optimal LLM model for future implementations.
ms.report:
Please see the linked video walking through the Milestone 3 PDF report
In this report you'll find:
・Reviews of LLMs across the spectrum of large, closed-source models to small, open-source models
・Use cases and tasks focused on proposers, reviewers and voters
・Optimal LLM choice based on our three approaches of 1) Academic reviews 2) Quantitative Experiments and 3) Qualitative Comparisons
